complexRules.name: Leeching Gland behavior
complexRules.description: The thrown gland rebounds and splits into four homing mini-glands. A hit fills the Survivor’s meter to Leeched I but does not exceed that threshold.

complexRules.name: Leeched II effects
complexRules.description: Leeched II automatically progresses from Leeched I; at the threshold, a healthy Survivor is injured and all health states receive Broken.

complexRules.name: Head-form Pallet interaction
complexRules.description: The Krasue vaults rather than breaks Pallets in Head form, cannot gain Bloodlust in that form, and is stunned for 2.5 seconds by a Pallet.

complexRules.name: Leeched progression
complexRules.description: Before Leeched I, Intestinal Whip adds 34 Charges and Regurgitate adds 100 Charges; neither Power hit can advance the meter beyond Leeched I. Once Leeched I is reached, the meter passively fills toward Leeched II at 1.665 charges per second, and Intestinal Whip becomes damaging.

complexRules.name: Headlong Flight behavior
complexRules.description: Headlong Flight is physical movement with Survivor collision. It can perform a vault, which ends the Flight; the tracker does not assign an undocumented damage effect to simple Survivor contact.

complexRules.name: Dynamic Glowing Fungus spawning
complexRules.description: A Body-to-Head transition can spawn a Glowing Fungus when The Krasue is at least 5 metres from interactable objects and other Fungi and is below the six-Fungus cap. Consumed Fungi can be replaced after 90 seconds.

complexRules.name: Head-form vault timing conflict
complexRules.description: Official 9.2.1 notes list 2.0-second Pallet and 1.8-second Window vaults, while the maintained current reference lists 1.9 and 1.67 seconds. Exact vault timings are optional/helper scope and are omitted from tracker mechanics rather than forcing a disputed value.

baselineFacts: The Krasue has Body and Head forms with distinct abilities.
Body-to-Head transition takes 1.2 seconds; Head-to-Body takes 2.2 seconds.
Headlong Flight has 12 charges, requires 25% charge to activate, and moves at 7 m/s.
Leeched progresses through two thresholds; Leeched II causes injury to healthy Survivors and Broken.
Exact Head-form Pallet and Window vault timings are omitted from tracker core because official 9.2.1 and the maintained current reference conflict.

power.characterName: Henry Creel (also known as One; often called Vecna)
power.shortSummary: The First uses Vine Attack and Undergate Attack to build Worldbreaker tokens on Survivors. Once Worldbreaker activates, those attacks damage instead of adding tokens, while Survivors can use Grandfather Clocks to shorten its first phase. The Upside Down provides fast, Undetectable traversal; token thresholds, Worldbreaker timing, Undergate effects, and Mind Break conditions are key Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation:
Vine Attack charges in 0.4 seconds and creates a ground area that gives a caught Survivor one Worldbreaker Token outside Worldbreaker. The First can also enter The Upside Down, becoming Undetectable, moving at 8 m/s and phasing through Pallets, Windows and Breakable Walls; Undergate Attack exits that state and gives caught Survivors two Tokens outside Worldbreaker. Each Survivor can hold up to four Tokens. Worldbreaker activates under any of three documented conditions: a Survivor reaches 2 Tokens, reaches 4 Tokens, or a Survivor already at 4 Tokens is hit by Vine Attack or Undergate Attack. During Worldbreaker those Power attacks deal damage instead of adding Tokens.

Worldbreaker Phase One lasts 60 seconds per living Survivor and can be accelerated by four Grandfather Clocks; Phase Two lasts 50 seconds. A Survivor who has reached Hook Stage 2 and has four Worldbreaker Tokens is eligible for Mind Break. If Vine or Undergate damage would put that Survivor into the Dying State during Worldbreaker, they are suspended for 15 seconds and The First can perform the Mind Break Mini-Mori.

components.name: Vine Attack
components.description: Charges and creates a ground area. Outside Worldbreaker, Survivors caught in it gain one Worldbreaker token; during Worldbreaker, the attack deals damage.

components.name: The Upside Down
components.description: A fast traversal state that grants Undetectable and ignores collision with Pallets, Windows, and Breakable Walls.

components.name: Undergate Attack
components.description: The First creates an expanding ground area and returns from The Upside Down. Outside Worldbreaker, it applies two tokens to Survivors caught in the area; during Worldbreaker, it deals damage.

components.name: Worldbreaker
components.description: Changes both attacks from token application to damage and starts a two-phase timer. Grandfather Clocks shorten the first phase.

components.name: Grandfather Clocks
components.description: Four clocks become interactable during Worldbreaker Phase One and accelerate its countdown.

components.name: Mind Break
components.description: A Survivor who has reached Hook Stage 2 and has four Tokens can be suspended instead of put into the Dying State by a qualifying Power hit during Worldbreaker; The First can then perform the Mini-Mori.

baselineFacts: Vine Attack adds one token; Undergate Attack adds two outside Worldbreaker.
Survivors can accumulate up to four tokens.
The Upside Down grants 8 m/s movement and Undetectable; its cooldown is 35 seconds after exit.
Four Grandfather Clocks can shorten Worldbreaker Phase One.
Worldbreaker Phase Two currently lasts 50 seconds.
Worldbreaker can activate when a Survivor reaches 2 Tokens, reaches 4 Tokens, or a 4-Token Survivor is hit by Vine Attack or Undergate Attack.

recentChanges.change: Reduced Worldbreaker Phase Two from 60 to 50 seconds.
recentChanges.verification: Official 9.5.0 notes state the revised timer. No later material base Power change was found through live version 10.2.0.

verificationNotes: The current maintained reference specifies the Worldbreaker activation details; official 9.4.0 notes describe activation after a Survivor has gained enough tokens but do not state the exact threshold in that passage.
Official 9.5.0 notes establish the current 50-second Phase Two timer.
Vine charge is 0.4 s. The 0.33 s figure is limited to reverted 9.5.0 PTB early-audio-cue wording.

Mind Break is keyed to having reached Hook Stage 2. A Survivor can reach that stage without necessarily having been hooked twice, so the compiled record does not translate the condition into hook-instance count.
Unpublished Undergate absolute radius and undocumented Token decay/retrigger behavior are omitted rather than encoded as negative facts.

power.shortSummary: The Slasher enters Omnipresent Evil to move quickly, become invisible and track Survivors through Mist Clouds or Footprints. Jump Scare ends the mode by moving him to a nearby Pallet, Breakable Wall, or Window; Throwing Spikes injure and push Survivors, with Hook Spikes adding impalement effects. Stealth duration, detection range, Jump Scare recovery, Spike handling, and impalement interactions are key Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation:
Omnipresent Evil makes The Slasher invisible and Undetectable, raises movement speed to 8 m/s and lets him pass through Pallets, Windows and Breakable Walls. In this state he cannot attack Survivors, cannot see Survivors or Scratch Marks, and cannot hear Survivors except Generator-repair noise. Instead, he senses Survivors within 16 metres through Mist Clouds and Footprints; remaining crouched long enough avoids the sensing system. After two seconds, Jump Scare can target a Pallet, Window or Breakable Wall within 16 metres. Reappearing normally takes 1.5 seconds, or 4.5 seconds near a hooked Survivor; the target Pallet/Window can be Entity-blocked for four seconds, while a Breakable Wall is destroyed. Jump Scare grants 4.5454% Haste for 25 seconds and nearby Killer Instinct for four seconds.

Throwing Spikes remove one Health State and push Survivors. A pushed Survivor colliding with another Survivor can injure a Healthy teammate or inflict Deep Wound on an Injured teammate. A Healthy Survivor hit by a Hook Spike becomes Impaled and Broken until the Spike is removed; removal takes five seconds normally and applies 10% Hindered during the removal interaction. A Spike hit that puts a Survivor into the Dying State and pushes them into a wall can Pin them. A Pinned Survivor automatically unpins after eight seconds and enters the Dying State, while a teammate rescue leaves them Injured. Ten Scrap Piles provide regular Spikes; activating Omnipresent Evil replenishes depleted Scrap Piles and repairs Hooks disabled by Hook-Spike reloads.

complexRules.name: Omnipresent Evil tracking
complexRules.description: The Slasher cannot see Survivors or Scratch Marks in the mode. Stationary Survivors produce Mist Clouds, while moving Survivors produce Footprints; crouching for over 2.5 seconds prevents sensing.

complexRules.name: Spike effect depends on Spike and collision
complexRules.description: A Hook Spike impales. A regular Spike damages and pushes; an Injured Survivor pushed into a wall can become pinned and immobilized.

complexRules.name: Conditional Mini-Mori
complexRules.description: A final-Hook or Finisher-Mori-eligible Survivor must remain pinned or impaled and be downed before The Slasher can perform the Power kill.

complexRules.name: Jump Scare near a hooked Survivor
complexRules.description: Reappearing takes three times as long when the target object is within 16 metres of a hooked Survivor; this is 4.5 seconds based on the 1.5-second normal time.

complexRules.name: Omnipresent Evil restrictions
complexRules.description: While in Omnipresent Evil, The Slasher cannot attack Survivors, cannot see Survivors or Scratch Marks, and cannot hear Survivors except Generator-repair noise. Tracking instead uses the 16-metre Mist Cloud/Footprint sensing system.

complexRules.name: Spike outcomes
complexRules.description: A normal Spike hit removes one Health State and pushes. A Healthy Survivor hit by a Hook Spike becomes Impaled. A Spike that puts a Survivor into the Dying State and pushes them into a wall can Pin them. A pushed Survivor colliding with another Survivor can injure a Healthy collateral target or apply Deep Wound to an Injured one.

baselineFacts: Omnipresent Evil grants 8 m/s movement, invisibility, and Undetectable.
Survivors within 16 metres are sensed through Mist Clouds or Footprints; crouching for over 2.5 seconds prevents sensing.
Jump Scare becomes available after two seconds and has a 12-second cooldown after use.
A Hook Spike impales and prevents healing beyond Injured until removed.
A final-Hook Survivor can be killed if downed while still pinned or impaled.

power.shortSummary: The Judgment directs Divine Light, then casts it as a damaging column that applies Heresy. Heretics suffer special Generator Skill Checks and can Repent at Shrines; downed Heretics can be sent to Exile, which gives The Judgment Zealous and gives Survivors rescue and item interactions. Divine Light timing, curve window, Heresy, Exile hazards, Shrines, and Zealous effects are key Add-on baselines.
power.fullExplanation:
The Judgment controls Divine Light for up to three seconds, then casts it as a damaging column that passes through obstacles, applies Heresy and uses a 6-second cooldown. The cast delay shortens from 0.9 to 0.3 seconds as it is controlled; a near miss within 0.5 metres can reveal the Survivor with Killer Instinct for two seconds. Survivors afflicted with Heresy are Heretics. Heresy can come from a Divine Light hit or qualifying taunts, including three crouches/gestures within 10 metres or 45 seconds in an Exit Threshold. Heretics receive special Generator Skill Checks; a Good result removes 3% Generator progress. Repenting at a Shrine begins the 30-second Heresy-removal process.

Seven Shrines of Judgment spawn. A Dying Heretic can be sent to Exile, which grants a Hook Stage and drains it at Hook rate but does not trigger Hook-related Perks. When a Survivor is Exiled, the two closest Shrines activate for liberation, and other Heretics whose Heresy is not being removed are revealed by Killer Instinct for three seconds. Inside Exile, Seeds of Punishment remove three seconds of Hook-Stage progress per hit, while up to ten Exiled Souls can be collected to add 0.5 seconds each to liberation protections before all Generators are completed. Liberation returns the Survivor 8–16 metres from a Shrine and at least 32 metres from The Judgment, with one second of Divine Light immunity. Exiling a Survivor grants Zealous for 60 seconds: Divine Light is 10% larger, has 20% less cooldown, its damaging cast lasts 50% longer, and it can curve for 0.6 seconds. Curving is Zealous-only in the current post-10.1.2 server-side state.

complexRules.name: Divine Light delay and control
complexRules.description: The cast delay shortens and the damaging duration lengthens as The Judgment controls Divine Light longer; the column does not damage during its controlled phase.

complexRules.name: Heresy and Exile
complexRules.description: Heresy can be gained by a hit or taunt. A downed Heretic can be Exiled; Exile grants a Hook Stage but does not trigger Hook-related perks.

complexRules.name: Zealous curve-window source history
complexRules.description: Current behavior is a 0.6-second curve window while Zealous only. 10.1.1 raised it to 0.6 seconds; 10.1.2 briefly raised it to 0.8 and added non-Zealous curving; the September 17 server-side correction restored 0.6 and removed non-Zealous curving.

complexRules.name: Final-Hook kill
complexRules.description: A downed Heretic on final Hook Stage can be killed instead of sent to Exile; Exiling or killing a final-stage Heretic activates Zealous.

complexRules.name: Heresy representation
complexRules.description: The tracker records the documented Heretic state and its triggers/effects without asserting an undocumented Heresy stack/tier model or declaring the system definitively binary; official 10.1.0 language includes 'full Heresy' without defining numeric tiers.

complexRules.name: Exile versus Hook
complexRules.description: Exile grants and drains a Hook Stage like a Hook state but does not trigger Hook-related Perks. Liberation has its own protection and return rules.

baselineFacts: Divine Light can be controlled for up to three seconds and has a six-second cooldown.
The cast delay ranges from 0.9 to 0.3 seconds based on control time.
Heresy comes from a hit or taunt; Heretics have special Generator Skill Checks and can Repent at one of seven Shrines.
Exiling a Survivor activates two nearby Shrines and gives The Judgment 60 seconds of Zealous.
The current Zealous curve window is 0.6 seconds after the September 17 server-side correction associated with 10.1.2.

recentChanges.change: Increased the Divine Light curve window while Zealous from 0.3 to 0.6 seconds.
recentChanges.verification: Official patch notes.

recentChanges.change: Reverted the Zealous curve window to 0.6 seconds after a temporary 0.8-second value, and removed the temporary 0.3-second non-Zealous curve window. Also set liberated Survivors’ return distance and Divine Light immunity.
recentChanges.verification: Official patch notes; 10.2.0 and 10.2.1 add bug fixes but no further material base Power change.

recentChanges.change: Restored the Zealous Divine Light curve window to 0.6 seconds and removed the temporary non-Zealous curve window.
recentChanges.verification: Official 10.1.2 patch page includes the subsequent server-side revert; current live behavior remains 0.6 seconds, Zealous only.

verificationNotes: The maintained reference provides the detailed taunt conditions and Shrine interaction values; official release notes support the core Heresy, Exile, and Zealous rules.
The current Zealous curve window is 0.6 seconds; the temporary 0.8-second value and non-Zealous curve window were reverted in the 10.1.2 hotfix.
The 10.2.0 patch contains Judgment bug fixes, not a material base Power change.
The tracker does not encode Heresy as definitively binary or invent Great/failed special Skill Check outcomes. Seed probability/cadence and Searcher's Pendant geometry remain helper-level.

addons.name: Heretic's Mark
addons.effect: When a cast Divine Light passes within 1 m of a Survivor without hitting them, that Survivor is revealed by Killer Instinct for 2 seconds.
addons.notes: Documented: in-game text gives 1 m and 2 s. Documented: base kit gives a 0.5 m / 2 s near-miss reveal behind a Beta setting (ON by default); equipping Heretic's Mark forces the setting ON (BHVR 10.1.0). Inference, not asserted in effect: the Add-on widens the base 0.5 m threshold to 1 m. 10.2.0 fixed near-miss Killer Instinct triggering on hiding Survivors (base-kit fix, no value change).
conflictNotes: Source A: wiki directly supports the wording 'within 1 m ... Killer Instinct for 2 s'. Source B: BHVR 10.1.0 notes (bugreport.deadbydaylight.com, 25 Aug 2026) describe the base near-miss reveal at 0.5 m and say equipping Heretic's Mark sets the setting to ON; they do not mention a 1 m value. INFERENCE (not established): the Add-on widens the base 0.5 m threshold to 1 m without stacking. Decision: effect wording kept as directly supported; inference not asserted. Confidence: medium. needsVerification true.

AUDIT 2026-10-16: Resolved. The 1 m / 2 s player-facing effect is first-party (in-game text). Internal replace-versus-widen semantics are undocumented implementation detail, not a material open fact. Confidence: high.
